correctness.rationale: In a linear-order game with t moves left, gaps either match below 2^t−1 or both meet that threshold. Playing the two coordinate games simultaneously clips each side at seven and preserves selected-pair equality and both strict inequalities, hence their conjunction, including plays with a repeated coordinate or pair. Terminal diagrams with all three variables and the iterated sets of extensions encode exactly three-round equivalence, not counts of responses. The independent replay `python3 audit-evidence/strict_grids.py` checked all 28 clipped unordered grids and matched equality of types iff equality of the claimed keys. Only the clipped (7,7) grid has its type, so any member of that class has both sides at least seven. This proves the sharp 49-point bound; the replay does not itself prove the infinite reduction.
